events.factual_description: Blue Note Japan presents the fourth JAZZ-FUSION SUMMIT at Kanadevia Hall on November 1, 2026, with doors at 2:00 PM and a 3:00 PM start. The official lineup comprises the Blue Note Tokyo All-Star Jazz Orchestra directed by Eric Miyashiro, T-SQUARE, DIMENSION, 本田雅人BAND, and a special trio of 沖仁 with 小沼ようすけ and 石塚隆充. The event page identifies 2026 as DIMENSION's 35th anniversary year and lists the current T-SQUARE personnel. The All-Star Jazz Orchestra roster is not yet final; Blue Note Japan explicitly marks additional members TBA. Standard ticket categories are sold out on the current official page, with some obstructed-view or standing inventory shown as remaining.

en.why_it_matters: The argument is the one-day cross-section of Japanese fusion rather than festival scale by itself: a newly constituted T-SQUARE, DIMENSION in its 35th-anniversary year, a player-heavy Masato Honda band, the Blue Note Tokyo all-star orchestra, and a flamenco-centered trio built around Jin Oki, Yosuke Onuma and Takamitsu Ishizuka. That mix makes the afternoon a useful snapshot of how virtuosity, groove and instrumental identity are circulating across generations in Japan right now.
en.trip_verdict: If November 1 overlaps a Tokyo stay, actively make room for the afternoon and let Kanadevia Hall anchor the day. Current standard inventory is sold out, so access should be verified through an authorized channel before reorganizing the rest of the itinerary.

es.why_it_matters: El argumento está en la fotografía de un solo día de la fusión japonesa, no en el tamaño del festival por sí mismo: un T-SQUARE reconstituido, DIMENSION en su año 35, una banda de Masato Honda cargada de instrumentistas, la orquesta all-star de Blue Note Tokyo y un trío centrado en flamenco con Jin Oki, Yosuke Onuma y Takamitsu Ishizuka. Esa mezcla vuelve la tarde una buena muestra de cómo están circulando hoy en Japón el virtuosismo, el groove y la identidad instrumental entre distintas generaciones.
es.trip_verdict: Si el 1 de noviembre coincide con una estancia en Tokio, sí le haría espacio activamente a la tarde y dejaría que Kanadevia Hall ordene el día. El inventario estándar aparece agotado en este momento, así que confirmaría acceso por un canal autorizado antes de reorganizar el resto del itinerario.

events.subtitle: Will Miller's electronic chamber-jazz project
lineup: Kenneth Charles Leftridge Jr. — saxophone, EWI
events.factual_description: Ars Nova Workshop presents Resavoir at Solar Myth on November 20, 2026 at 8:00 PM. The official page confirms Will Miller on EVI, keys and trumpet; Lane Beckstrom on bass and sampler; Jeremy Cunningham on drums and SPD; and Kenneth Charles Leftridge Jr. on saxophone and EWI. It describes Resavoir as a project whose live format can range from a 17-piece orchestra to solo performance and situates this appearance after the release of the meditative full-length Themes For Dreams. The show is seated and listed at $22 advance / $25 day of show, age 21+.

enrichment.note: Date, time, complete announced quartet, instrumentation, seated format, price and authorized DICE destination are verified from Ars Nova Workshop. No exact Apple Music destination is supplied without verification.

sources.note: Primary presenter page verifying November 20, 2026 at 8:00 PM, Solar Myth, complete quartet instrumentation, seated format, price and authorized DICE ticket link.

en.why_it_matters: The live configuration is the reason to keep this on RADAR: trumpet and EVI share the front line with saxophone and EWI, while sampler, bass, acoustic drums and SPD make the rhythm section partly electronic. Resavoir can change scale radically from tour to tour, so this specific quartet offers a compact way to hear Miller's arranging instinct as instrumental color rather than a fixed jazz-band format.
en.trip_verdict: Catch it if a Friday in Philadelphia is already workable; the quartet is distinctive enough to reward a Solar Myth night, but I would pair it with another reason for the corridor trip rather than make it the only anchor.

es.why_it_matters: La razón para ponerlo en RADAR es la configuración en vivo: trompeta y EVI comparten el frente con saxofón y EWI, mientras sampler, bajo, batería acústica y SPD vuelven parcialmente electrónica a la sección rítmica. Resavoir puede cambiar radicalmente de escala entre giras, así que este cuarteto concreto permite escuchar el instinto de arreglista de Miller como color instrumental y no como un formato fijo de banda de jazz.
es.trip_verdict: La aprovecharía si un viernes en Filadelfia ya resulta viable; el cuarteto es suficientemente distintivo para justificar una noche en Solar Myth, pero lo combinaría con otra razón para hacer el viaje por el corredor en vez de convertirlo en el único ancla.

events.subtitle: Current EVERYDAY-era group at Blue Note Tokyo
events.factual_description: Blue Note Tokyo presents Takuya Kuroda on November 26 and 27, 2026, with sets at 6:00 PM and 8:30 PM each night. The venue confirms Kuroda on trumpet with Craig Hill on saxophone, Takahiro Izumikawa on piano and keyboards, and Reuben Cainer on bass; additional personnel remain TBA. Blue Note Tokyo frames the return around Kuroda's current EVERYDAY era and notes the album's nomination for MUSIC AWARDS JAPAN 2026 Best Jazz Album. The listed music charge is ¥9,500.

en.why_it_matters: Kuroda's current language has a concrete instrumental center: trumpet and saxophone ride over a keyboard-and-bass foundation built to absorb Afrobeat, R&B and hip-hop without losing the elasticity of a jazz group. With EVERYDAY now carrying a visible Japanese awards context, these two Tokyo nights offer a useful snapshot of the Brooklyn-based trumpeter's present sound rather than a retrospective or prestige booking.
en.trip_verdict: Attend if November 26 or 27 fits naturally into a Tokyo stay; four sets across two nights make this easy to place around rarer anchors rather than forcing the itinerary to revolve around it.

es.why_it_matters: El lenguaje actual de Kuroda tiene un centro instrumental concreto: trompeta y saxofón se montan sobre una base de teclados y bajo capaz de absorber afrobeat, R&B y hip-hop sin perder la elasticidad de un grupo de jazz. Con EVERYDAY ahora dentro de una conversación visible en los premios japoneses, estas dos noches en Tokio funcionan como una buena fotografía del sonido presente del trompetista radicado en Brooklyn, no como retrospectiva ni como booking de prestigio.
es.trip_verdict: Iría si el 26 o 27 de noviembre embona naturalmente en una estancia en Tokio; cuatro sets en dos noches dan suficiente flexibilidad para acomodarlo alrededor de anclas más raras sin hacer que todo el itinerario gire alrededor de esta fecha.
